Good afternoon Senator Tipping, Chair Roeder and the other distinguished members of the Joint Standing Committee on Labor. l am Bill Brown, Director of Actuarial and Legislative Affairs for the Maine Public Employees Retirement System (MainePERS).
MainePERS is neither for nor against LD 1638, An Act Regarding Disability Retirement Benefits
Under the Maine Public Employees Retirement System. We are here to provide information and
to offer any assistance the committee may request regarding this bill.
In addition to its primary service retirement programs MainePERS also administers a Disability Retirement Program. Disability Retirement serves members who become unable to work but are not yet ready or eligible to start their service retirement benefit. As a form of retirement, it is a
unique benefit that has different requirements under Maine law than other similar but different
government-run disability programs. it is also different than private insurance that may be purchased to provide some income during a short-term or long-term illness that prevents someone from working.
According to statute, in order to qualify for Disability Retirement a member must demonstrate
that one or more medically diagnosable conditions exist, that functional limitations caused by those conditions make the member unable to perform the essential functions of the member's employment position with reasonable accommodation and that the inability can be expected to be permanent.

The great majority of MainePERS members do not participate in Social Security. Those that do are typically members of the Participating Local District (PLD) Consolidated Plan, working for
cities, towns, counties or local utilities like water or sanitary districts. Under arrangements
reached by their employers, some of these members contribute to both MainePERS and to
Social Security.

Under Maine law, when these members apply for and receive disability retirement benefits through MainePERS and Social Security for the same disabling condition and period of employment, a portion of their MainePERS benefit is offset by the benefit received from Social
Security. A similar provision exists in statute for the StatelTeacher plan but it is not triggered as
State/Teacher members do not pay into Social Security.

The amount of disability retirement benefit available through MainePERS generally is 59% of a member's Average Final Compensation (AFC). If the member is also receiving Social Security disability benefits for the same disability and period of employment, the MainePERS disability benefit is reduced so that the two benefits combined do not exceed 80% of the member's predisability compensation taking into account AFC and wages and earnings from other
employment.

LD 1638 seeks to eliminate the offset of MainePERS disability retirement benefits by Social Security benefits received for the same condition. The bill also proposes the retroactive payment of previously offset benefits plus cost-of-living adjustments (COLA) and interest. The
proposed interest rate on these payments is prime rounded up to the nearest whole percent,
plus 3. Currently that is 10.5%. This greatly exceeds the 6.5% that MainePERS uses as an investment assumption for the trust funds. LD 1638 also eliminates the requirement that those
eligible to apply for disability benefits under Social Security do so before making application to MainePERS.

This bill will have a fiscal impact on the PLD Consolidated Plan because disability retirement
benefit recipients will receive higher benefits, thus increasing the actuarial liabilities of the Plan.
From a plan funding perspective, there is the expectation that some portion of disability
retirement benefits will be offset, and our actuaries have valued plan liabilities and recommended contribution rates based on our historic experience, which has included the effect of the offsets. If those offsets are eliminated, the actuary will determine the impact on future
actuarial liabilities and how plan costs are impacted.

The immediate costs of LD 1638 have not yet been determined. This is in part because the System would need to manually recalculate the retroactive benefits for current disability
retirement recipients for whom benefits are offset, as proposed in the bill. Additionally, our
actuaries would need to determine the immediate costs based on current recipients as well as the impact of changing the assumptions related to benefit offsets, as stated above.

As previously indicated, L.D. 1638 applies specifically to the PLD Consolidated Plan, which is
funded by participating municipalities and other local districts and their employees. The program is not funded by the State. In recognition of this, and pursuant to Title 5, Section 18801, subsection 2, amendments to retirement benefit statutes do not become part of the PLD plan unless adopted through rulemaking based on a recommendation of the PLD Advisory Committee. This Committee is established in statute with its voting membership evenly split between plan employers and employees.

Thank you for your consideration of this testimony. I am happy to take your questions and will
be present for any work session.

190749:
Professional Fire Fighters of Maine
Afliliated with the International Association of Fire Fighters
Testimony of Gerry Gay, 6"` District Vice President Tuesday, April 22, 2025
LD 1638 - "An Act Regarding Disability Retirement Benefits Under the Maine Public
Employees Retirement System"
Senator Tipping, Representative Roeder and other esteemed members of the Labor Committee.
My name is Gerry Gay, I served City of Sanford for 40 years as a career firefighter. I'm here to testify in support of LD 1638 as the 6*" District Vice President of the Professional Fire Fighters of
Maine, representing over 1,200 First Responders and their families across the State of Maine.
Thank you for this important opportunity to speak on behalf of the brave men and women who
serve as first responders.
I am here today to express my strong support for the bill that removes the reduction of disability
retirement benefits for individuals receiving benefits from both the Maine Public Employees Retirement System (MainePERS) and the United States Social Security Act (SSA).
Under current law, a person who is receiving disability retirement benefits from MainePERS sees
those benefits reduced if they are also receiving disability benefits from SSA. This policy creates
an unfair financial hardship for many disabled public employees who rely on these benefits to
support themselves and their families.
This bill provides crucial relief by eliminating the reduction for individuals who were receiving MainePERS disability retirement benefits as of December 31, 2024. It also ensures that these
individuals are retroactively compensated for any benefits that were withheld due to the reduction,
including any cost-of-living adjustments (COLAs) and interest. This retroactive provision is especially important, as it addresses the financial challenges that have been imposed on these
individuals over the years due to a policy that did not fully consider the needs of disabled public employees.
Furthermore, the bill eliminates the requirement for applicants to provide proof of applying for
SSA disability benefits as part of their application for MainePERS disability retirement. This change removes an unnecessary bureaucratic hurdle for disabled individuals, many of whom may
already be overwhelmed by the challenges of their disability and navigating multiple benefit
systems.
The impact of disability is often lifelong, and for many, the financial stability provided by
disability retirement benefits is essential to maintaining a basic standard of living. By passing this bill, we can correct an inequity that has placed undue stress on disabled public employees who have already sacrificed so much for the public good.
I urge the committee to support this important legislation and to stand up for the disabled public
servants who have devoted their careers to serving the State of Maine. This bill will go a long way
in ensuring that these individuals are treated with the dignity and respect they deserve.
Thank you for your time and I would be pleased to address any questions you may have.

April 22, 2025
Senator Tipping, Representative Roeder and members of the Joint Standing Committee on
Labor. My name is Jill Duson. I represent Senate District 27 which includes part of the City of
Westbrook and part of Portland. In addition, I have the honor of serving as the Senate Assistant
Majority Leader. I am pleased to present for your consideration, LD 1638, "An Act Regarding
Disability Retirement Benefits Under the Maine Public.Empl0yees Retirement System."
As you may know, the Social Security Fairness Act (Public Law No. 118-273) was signed into law by then President Biden on January 5th of this year. The SSFA which was passed on
overwhelmingly bipartisan votes in the House and the Senate repealed two tax provisions, the Windfall Elimination Provision (WEP) and the Government Pension Offset (GPO).
The Act repealed provisions that reduced Social Security benefits for individuals who receive
other benefits such as a pension from state or local government. It eliminated the pension offset
which reduced SS benefits for spouses, widows and widowers who also received govermnent pensions of their own. And, it eliminated the provision that reduced SS benefits for individuals who also receive a pension or disability benefit from an employer that did not withhold Social
Security taxes.
The SSFA repeal of these provisions restored earned Social Security benefits for more than 2 million retirees, including more than 25,000 retired Maine workers.
The bill before you, LD 1638, aims to correct similarly unfair offsets that result in a portion of
Maine Public Employee Retirement System (MainePERS) Disability benefits being withheld
from retired Maine workers who received Social Security Disability Insurance payments.
In 1991, the Maine Legislature created the MainePERS Social Security disability offset as part of a large Worker's Compensation reform bill. This offset reduced benefits to well below the defined disability benefit amount of 59% of Annual Final Compensation for a small group of MainePERS disabled retirees - those who worked in Social Security covered public service jobs fully paying into both Social Security and MainePERS.

Testimony in Support of LD 1638
Good afternoon, Sen. Tipping, Rep. Roeder, and to the members of the Labor Committee. My
name is Mark Evers. I live in Millinocket where I worked as a Fire Fighter/Paramedic for nearly
30 years.
I have been a MainePERS disabled retiree since I was injured at work and forced to retire in July
of 2022. I am testifying in support of LD 1638 to retroactively repeal the MainePERS Social Security disability offset. My monthly MainePERS disability pension is $440/month because of

Becoming disabled from a workplace injury greatly affected my quality of life. I am unable to
perform many daily tasks. I need to pay someone to do home repairs, vehicle maintenance, even
cutting the grass.
Having paid into both MePERS and Social Security in my "Social Security covered job" in the
Participating Local District retirement plan, it is very disheartening to not receive "full benefits"
from my contributions. Even the cost of health insurance, Medicare, a supplemental plan, and
drug coverage is significantly more than I ever paid while working.
All these added costs associated with being disabled, the burden would be greatly lessened if I was to receive all retirement income, which I earned, by doing away with the offset between
MePERS and Social Security disability.
When going to work, day after day, over the years, you are contributing to what you believe to be
programs that will take care of you when you retire or if something should happen. In reality, it is just an illusion. With the offset, you are not receiving the benefits you perceived would be there. In reality you are held to an income that is inadequate, considering all the added expenses that come with being disabled.
This bill repeals the MePERS Social Security disability offset and restores to me the money MainePERS deducted from my benefits over the past three years.
I urge the committee to vote unanimously Ought to Pass on LD l638.

Testimony in Support of LD 1638
An Act Regarding Disability Retirement Benefits

Good morning. Thank you for the opportunity to offer my testimony in support of this bill. My name is Thomas Gilman. I am 60 years old at this time. In late 2023, I had to leave my position
of 28 years in the City of Sanford Public Works Department due to a painful condition, DISH
Disease.
DISH stands for Diffuse Idiopathic Skeletal Hyperostosis, which is a form of arthritis that causes
soft tissue to stiffen and calcify (specifically your ligaments, tendons and joints, especially along the spine). (DISH and the associated musculoskeletal pain are also accompanied by mobility problems.) Soon after leaving work, I was approved for Social Security disability benefits and in
late May 2024 I began receiving MainePERS disability retirement benefits.
I need the money that has been underpaid from my MainePERS disability benefits due to the MainePERS Social Security offset. Just my medical costs have been staggering. I am on my
wife's insurance plan through her employer. Her insurance premium alone is $208.00 every two
weeks deducted from her pay. I maxed out my out-of-pocket costs for 2024.
There is no cure for DISH, only treatments aimed to relieve symptoms using physiotherapy. There is a surgery that could be an option for myself and others with this
condition but my doctors have advised me that there is only a 50-50 chance of gaining any relief; the other 50% chance is that I would not be able to walk again. Every six months or so I can
have an ablation procedure that relieves some of the pain caused by calcification. But before I
can have this procedure, I have to have two tests and my doctor has to authorize the tests to
appease the insurance company. The out-of-pocket costs are $400+ each test.
Just in this short time since leaving work, our mortgage has fallen behind and we struggle and juggle to try to stay on track. Through my employer, the City of Sanford, I paid into both MainePERS and Social Security. I never thought that I would be denied the full MainePERS benefit I paid for. This offset may not have been done deliberately to punish us for becoming
disabled, but it is extremely important to us all that this unfair situation be corrected--for the sake
of us and most importantly for our spouses and family members who take care of us. Please
support this bill which restores equity in the system and addresses the underpayment of our
benefits.
And sadly, as an afterthought, my wife adds that because I am a MainePERS disabled retiree, ifl pass before she does, she may not receive any benefit from my pension. This is not what we saw, during my years as a public employee, for our family's future. This is not howl intended to take care of my spouse.
Thank you for considering my testimony. I urge the committee to pass this bill with the
retroactivity clause releasing our withheld funds. Please vote unanimously Ought to Pass.
